headline_cluster.headline: "אני לא יכול לעבוד באופן ספייס": 160 אלף איש התאיידו משוק העבודה

primary_source_search_status: not_found_as_published_figure: no CBS / Bank of Israel / ministry / think-tank publication stating '160,000' was found in Hebrew or English search. The figure first appears in TheMarker's own 2026-07-29 article and is most consistent with an outlet-derived counterfactual: (pre-war labor-force participation rate 63.9%, Sep 2023 - current CBS Labor Force Survey rate) x population aged 15+. Reference points located: CBS LFS Feb 2025 62.6% (-1.3pp, reported as ~95k fewer participants, tv10.co.il/israel/26856); June 2026 ~62.0-62.3%; July 2026 62.2%; August 2026 61.8% (-2.1pp vs 63.9%, ~150-160k at ~7.3-7.5M pop 15+). Ice/Bank-of-Israel-cited decomposition: ~55% of the employment-rate decline from lower participation, ~35-36% from reservists/partners absent from civilian work. Searched: themarker headline phrases, CBS LFS 2026 monthly releases, BoI annual report ch.5 2025, Taub labor 2024, English re-reports.
clustering_note: Single-outlet TheMarker weekend-magazine feature (paywalled .highlight). The same URL is indexed under a different title: '"הבן שלי מת ואתה מדבר איתי על הובלה שלא הגיעה?": 160 אלף הישראלים שנעלמו משוק העבודה' - i.e. a human-interest follow-up (bereaved parents, reservists etc.) to TheMarker's own 2026-07-29 macro piece '160 אלף איש שנעלמו משוק העבודה הופכים לבעיה הכי מדאיגה במשק' (alt title: 'לא מבינים מה קורה פה: לאן, לכל הרוחות, נעלמו 160 אלף עובדים?') and related to the 2026-07-02 TheMarker career piece 'רבע מיליון ישראלים נעלמו משוק העבודה'. Headline quote 'אני לא יכול לעבוד באופן ספייס' = 'I can't work in an open space (open-plan office)' - an interviewee quote, framing only, not a claim. Body not fetched (WebFetch egress-blocked; paywall); body content known only from search-engine snippets.

claims.source_figure: No published 160,000 figure. CBS LFS participation rate fell from 63.9% (eve of war, Sep 2023) to 61.8% (Aug 2026) = -2.1pp; at a 15+ population of ~7.3-7.5M this implies ~150-160k fewer labor-force participants than at the pre-war rate. Earlier comparable estimate: -1.3pp = ~95k (Feb 2025).
claims.note: Order of magnitude is reproducible from CBS data (with Aug-2026 data), so not unsupported, but the headline gives no baseline, method or date. The number is a counterfactual (participation-rate gap x population), not a count of people who left jobs; it bundles composition effects (growing Haredi share - the July piece says the sharpest decline is among Haredi men; ageing), prolonged studies and reservist effects. 'התאיידו' (evaporated) implies identifiable individuals exiting. Notably the 160k figure was already used on 2026-07-29 when the June/July rates (62.0-62.3%) implied only ~120-140k, so the exact computation basis is unverified. TheMarker's own July article called the phenomenon unexplained and spanning three years, whereas the weekend feature's framing (bereavement, war trauma) attaches it to Oct 7 specifically - causal framing not separately verdicted (framing), but it narrows a multi-cause aggregate into a war-trauma story.

claims.claim_text: בין 160 אלף ל-250 אלף ישראלים יצאו משוק העבודה מאז 7 באוקטובר
claims.source_figure: Lower bound: see claim 1. Upper bound 250,000: traced only to TheMarker's own paywalled 2026-07-02 piece ('רבע מיליון ישראלים נעלמו משוק העבודה'); no primary source located.
claims.note: Multilingual search found no CBS/BoI/institutional estimate of ~250k labor-market exits since Oct 7. The 160k-250k spread itself signals a loose estimate. Body text seen only through search snippets, so wording may differ.

audit_note: Partial: article body unreadable (paywall + WebFetch egress block); claims reconstructed from search snippets. Primary CBS LFS data located via secondary re-reports, not read directly from cbs.gov.il. Worst verdict: imprecise (headline). Not yet blind-QA'd.
